extracted.intended_audience: graduate students and researchers in algebraic topology (studying obstruction theory, Postnikov/Moore–Postnikov towers, and lifting/extension problems)
extracted.subtask_description: Determine existence (and compute) extensions or lifts of maps between CW complexes and fibrations by building Postnikov / Moore–Postnikov towers and extracting obstruction classes in cohomology. Includes criteria for well-definedness of obstructions and special cases giving existence results.

rubrics_metrics.name: Extension problem reduced to obstruction classes ωn
rubrics_metrics.description: Given a CW pair (W,A) and a map A → X, suppose X has a Postnikov tower. For each stage n one obtains an obstruction class ωn ∈ H^{n+1}(W ∪ CA; πnX) ≈ H^{n+1}(W,A; πnX) determined by the map W ∪ CA → K(πnX, n+1).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proposition 4.72: A lift W → Xn extending the given A → Xn exists iff ωn = 0. Practical procedure: attempt to lift inductively over Postnikov stages; at stage n the obstruction is the cohomology class coming from W ∪ CA → K and must vanish to extend the lift. (Text gives explicit construction: nullhomotopy of W→K extending the nullhomotopy on A corresponds to vanishing of ωn.)

rubrics_metrics.name: Relative lifting problem obstructions
rubrics_metrics.description: For a fibration p: X→Y with fiber F and a CW pair (W,A) and map W→Y (with given lift on A), there is a sequence of obstructions ωn ∈ H^{n+1}(W,A; πnF) whose vanishing at each stage is necessary and (in the inductive sense used) sufficient for producing a lift W→X extending the given lift on A.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assume the fibration has a Moore–Postnikov tower of principal fibrations; then proceed stage-by-stage. Note the special proviso that π1F should be abelian in the case n = 1. Existence of a lift corresponds to finding successive nullhomotopies (as in the extension problem) with obstructions lying in twisted cohomology groups with coefficients πnF.

rubrics_metrics.name: Vanishing cohomology groups give automatic extendability (Corollary 4.73)
rubrics_metrics.description: If X is a connected abelian CW complex and (W,A) is a CW pair such that H^{n+1}(W,A; πnX) = 0 for all n, then every map A → X can be extended to a map W → X.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is an immediate application of the obstruction-stage vanishing: if every obstruction group is zero then every ωn must vanish and the inductive lifting procedure succeeds. This is a stronger, cohomological criterion than the elementary cell-by-cell vanishing of πn(X) for relevant dimensions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Principal Postnikov tower condition (when Postnikov tower can be taken principal)
rubrics_metrics.description: One can adjoin X0 (a point) and obtain an extended Postnikov tower of principal fibrations when π1(X) is abelian and acts trivially on all the higher homotopy groups of X.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Practical implication: when π1 is abelian and acts trivially, the Postnikov tower stages Xn → Xn−1 are principal fibrations (e.g. X1 is K(π1X,1) which is the loopspace of K(π1X,2)). This principal structure is used to identify obstructions in ordinary cohomology groups rather than requiring twisted coefficient complications.

rubrics_metrics.name: Well-definedness of obstructions requires connectivity hypotheses on fiber
rubrics_metrics.description: Although Proposition 4.72 is an iff statement for the individual stage, the sequence of obstruction classes ωn may depend on choices of lifts: even if ωn = 0 and a lift to Zn+1 exists, different choices of such a lift can produce different subsequent ωn+1's. A simple case with well-defined primary obstruction is when πi(F) = 0 for i < n, so the Moore–Postnikov factorization begins with Zn and the primary obstruction ωn ∈ H^{n+1}(W,A; πnF) is well-defined.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Interpretation guidance: do not assume vanishing of the constructed obstructions is necessary in full generality for existence of a lift unless you are in a situation (connectivity of fiber up to stage n−1, or other special hypotheses) guaranteeing uniqueness of choices. Expect ambiguities to accumulate with successive choices of lifts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Lifting to first stage Z1 via covering space criterion
rubrics_metrics.description: Z1 may be taken as the covering space of Y corresponding to the subgroup p_*(π1(X)) ⊂ π1(Y). Covering-space theory determines when W → Y lifts to Z1: existence and the ability to choose a lift agreeing with a given lift on A depend on whether the induced maps on π1 factor through the subgroup; potential issues occur when A has more than one component.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use standard covering-space lifting criteria (lifting exists iff the image of π1 of the domain lies in the subgroup corresponding to the cover). Uniqueness (or the compatibility with an existing lift on A) may fail across components, so check component-wise conditions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Using mapping cylinders to make maps inclusions when building towers
rubrics_metrics.description: When arranging successive stages X → Zn+1 → Zn → Y one may replace maps by inclusions by taking mapping cylinders (first of X→Zn+1, then of new Zn+1→Zn, then of Zn→Y). This lets one view homotopy fibers of inclusions and identify relative homotopy groups.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Technical guideline used in proofs: replace maps by cofibrations (inclusions) to make the homotopy fiber of an inclusion A ↪ B have π_i equal to π_{i+1}(B,A). This is convenient when checking the Moore–Postnikov / Postnikov conditions on relative homotopy groups.

rubrics_metrics.name: Homology isomorphism criterion for homotopy equivalence in abelian CW complexes (Proposition 4.74)
rubrics_metrics.description: If X and Y are connected abelian CW complexes, then a map f: X → Y inducing isomorphisms on all homology groups is a homotopy equivalence.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proof strategy uses obstruction theory: reduce to inclusion X ↪ Y, check triviality of π1(X) action on πn(Y,X), apply relative Hurewicz to deduce πn(Y,X)=0; use obstruction-theory-based extension of the identity to get a retraction Y → X. Practical use: for abelian (π1 acts trivially) CW complexes, homology data suffices to detect homotopy equivalence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Computation/construction of obstruction class via nullhomotopy on W ∪ CA
rubrics_metrics.description: A lift to Xn is equivalent to producing a nullhomotopy of the composite W → Xn−1 → K where K = K(πnX, n+1), and since we already have such a nullhomotopy on A, the pair gives a map W ∪ CA → K whose cohomology class is the obstruction ωn ∈ H^{n+1}(W ∪ CA; πnX).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Concrete recipe for computing ωn: form the map W ∪ CA → K determined by the given data and read off the obstruction in H^{n+1}(W,A; πnX). To show equivalence: ωn = 0 iff the map W ∪ CA → K is nullhomotopic, which is equivalent to existence of the required nullhomotopy on W and hence a lift.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ambiguity and non-necessity of obstruction vanishing in absence of uniqueness
rubrics_metrics.description: Even though Proposition 4.72 gives an iff at a single stage, the overall converse question (if a lift exists must all ωn be zero?) is subtle: different choices of intermediate lifts can change later obstructions, so vanishing of a canonical sequence of obstructions is only guaranteed under special circumstances (e.g., connectivity hypotheses).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Warning for practitioners: when verifying existence of lifts by checking a produced sequence of obstruction classes, be aware that failure of a particular constructed ωn to vanish need not preclude existence of some other lift; conversely, a lift's existence does not automatically imply the particular sequence you computed is identically zero unless choices are controlled.
